# Brief for Tuesday 27 October 2026, 17:45 UTC
Coverage window: since Sunday 25 October, 17:45 UTC. Prices differ slightly between sources because they sample at different times.

## Crude oil (Brent, WTI)
- **Prices, Monday 26 Oct:** Brent settled at $115.81 a barrel, down 91 cents, and WTI at about $101.76 (Arbiterz, 27 Oct). A price-data site instead shows Brent +3.21% and WTI +2.27% over one day at 21:06 UTC on 26 Oct (OilPriceAPI). I could not reconcile the two.
- **Prices, Tuesday 27 Oct:** Brent futures were down 0.86% at $114.80 and WTI down 0.76% at $101.00 (Arbiterz). Another report had Brent at $115.15 and WTI at $101.32 (Voice of Emirates).
- **Iran diplomacy, Monday 26 Oct:** Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan met Iranian officials in Tehran to discuss de-escalating the US-Iran war (FXEmpire). Iran, Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey agreed to keep talking. Oman said its talks with Iran produced an outline to restore free navigation in the Strait of Hormuz (MoneyCheck, 27 Oct).
- **Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia:** The Houthis said they attacked Saudi pipeline pumping stations and Riyadh airport (MoneyCheck, 27 Oct). This is the Houthis' own claim as reported there. Renewed attacks on Saudi territory and high tension in the Strait of Hormuz limited the price decline (Voice of Emirates, 27 Oct).
- **Context:** Brent topped $117 last week, its highest level since April (Voice of Emirates). OilPrice.com's headline says Brent holds near $115 as Iran war tensions and Saudi-Houthi hostilities keep markets on edge ahead of the US midterms (27 Oct).
- **US inventories:** There was no new weekly report inside the window. The latest EIA data, released 21 Oct, showed US commercial crude down 3.1 million barrels to 412.5 million in the week to 16 October. The next EIA release is Wednesday 28 October. The SPR was at about 282.7 million barrels, its lowest since October 1982 (global-energy-flow.com, using EIA data). I did not find the API figure due this evening.
- **OPEC+:** I found nothing new in the window.
- **Demand:** I found nothing new in the window.

## Gold
- **Price:** Spot was $4,015.37 an ounce at 9:00 a.m. ET on 26 Oct, slightly below Friday's $4,026.22 at the same time (CNBC). On 27 Oct at 17:32 UTC, BullionVault showed $4,062.79 an ounce.
- **Drivers:** A dealer's market report for 26 Oct said gold held just below $4,000 as a retreat in crude eased inflation worries that hit precious metals last week (USAGold). Traders were squaring positions ahead of Wednesday's Fed decision.
- Nothing else new found.

## US equities (S&P 500)
- **Monday 26 Oct close:** The Dow rose 0.28% to 52,361.58, the S&P 500 rose 0.7% to 7,676.77 and the Nasdaq rose 0.82% to 26,169.38 (CNBC). The report credited Anthropic's IPO filing with easing some fears around the AI trade. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq were coming off back-to-back weekly losses.
- **Strategist note:** RBC Capital Markets' Lori Calvasina said the S&P 500 could pull back 5% to 10% in the near term (CNBC, 26 Oct). She noted the index was down 2% from its 22 October peak.
- **Tuesday 27 Oct:** One page showed the S&P 500 at 7,720.49, up 0.6% (Motley Fool). It gave no timestamp, so I could not confirm a close. The Fed's two-day meeting began Tuesday and the week has heavy earnings, with attention on hyperscalers' capital spending (Benzinga).

## US Treasuries and the Fed
- **Yields, Tuesday 27 Oct:** The 10-year rose more than 1 basis point to 5.003% and the 30-year to 5.316%. The 2-year rose 3 basis points to 4.741% (CNBC).
- **Yields, Monday 26 Oct:** The 10-year was little changed at 4.986%, the 30-year was 5.299% and the 2-year was 4.716% (CNBC).
- **Fed meeting:** The two-day meeting began Tuesday, with the decision due Wednesday. Traders widely expect rates to stay at 3.75% to 4%, with roughly a 90% chance of a hold per CME FedWatch. They will look for clues on whether the Fed will hike again before year-end. The current range follows a 25-basis-point hike in September (Benzinga, 27 Oct).

Sources: CNBC, Arbiterz, FXEmpire, MoneyCheck, Voice of Emirates, OilPrice.com, OilPriceAPI, global-energy-flow.com, BullionVault, USAGold, Motley Fool, Benzinga. I used six searches, and the last one was spent on inventories and OPEC+.

# Paper-trading news brief, Wednesday 28 October 2026, 13:18 UTC
Window: since Monday 26 October, 13:18 UTC. No forecasts or advice. Source quality varies, and I flag conflicts where they appear.

## Crude oil (Brent, WTI)

- **Prices, 26–28 Oct.** One data feed shows Monday 26 Oct at WTI $101.44 and Brent $114.85, and at 00:51 UTC on 28 Oct at WTI $100.38 and Brent $114.47. (oilpriceapi.com, 28 Oct.) Kotak Neo's commodity research put Brent near $115 and WTI near $101, close to six-month highs. (Business Standard, 28 Oct.)
- **Source conflict.** Valor listed WTI $101.27 and Brent $110.08 as of 27 Oct. A worldoilmonitor.com page shows a "close" of $111.29 for 28 Oct, which can't be a settlement at this hour. Brent therefore ranges from about $110 to $115.6 across sources, and I could not confirm an official settlement.
- **Saudi infrastructure, 28 Oct.** Brent rose to $115.59 and WTI to $101.37 after the Houthis claimed a ballistic missile attack on the Ras Tanura refinery. (Traders Union, 28 Oct.) This is a claim only; I did not find independent confirmation.
- **Hormuz and Iran.**
  - On Tuesday 27 Oct, Iran reiterated that Hormuz could resume tanker traffic within four to five days if the US lifts its naval blockade and meets Tehran's demands, per Iranian state media cited by a tracker. (houseofsaud.com, 28 Oct; secondary source.)
  - Over the weekend, Iran's ambassador to Pakistan said Tehran had offered to restore shipping if Washington ended the blockade, but Tasnim denied a new offer had been delivered. (News Beep, 25 Oct.)
  - Qatar and Pakistan are mediating, which is temporarily capping Brent at about $115. (News Beep, undated; it was published within the last day.)
  - US Energy Secretary Wright said Persian Gulf oil flows have recovered to about 80% of pre-war levels, though refined-product shipments remain constrained. (Yahoo Finance, reported as said "on Monday".)
- **OPEC+.** OPEC+ is expected to hold December output targets steady at its Sunday meeting and to focus on 2027 quotas instead. (News Beep, 28 Oct.) Another source gives the meeting date as 1 November. No decision yet.
- **US inventories.** Nothing new found. The latest EIA report I found is from 21 Oct, before the window: a 3.1-million-barrel draw in the week ending 16 Oct, taking commercial stocks to 412.5 million barrels, 3% below the five-year average. (oilprice.com.) The next EIA report is due Wednesday 28 Oct, normally around 10:30 ET, and I found no coverage of it. I found no API figures for this week.
- **Demand.** Nothing new found.

## Gold

- **Prices.** On Monday 26 Oct, spot gold was holding just below $4,000 after a drop the previous week that the source tied to inflation worries and rate-hike fears. (USAGOLD.) GoldPrice.org shows a Monday close of $3,997.71.
- **Tuesday 27 Oct.** Kitco showed $4,059.00, up $42.80, as of 4:45 p.m. EDT, with a day range of $3,988.50 to $4,066.70.
- **28 Oct.** BullionVault showed about $4,047 per ounce at 02:03 GMT.
- **Drivers.** USAGOLD reported that traders were squaring positions ahead of Wednesday's Fed decision. I found no other gold-specific news (central banks, ETF flows) in this window.

## US equities (S&P 500)

- **Monday 26 Oct.** The S&P 500 was at 7,676.77, up 0.70%, per Schwab's midday update. That matches the previous close of 7,676.77 shown by CNBC.
- **Tuesday 27 Oct close.** The S&P 500 gained 0.60% to 7,722.60, the Nasdaq Composite rose 1.18% to 26,477.81, and the Dow rose 0.03% to 52,377.57. (TradingKey.) The drivers were chip-stock gains, falling oil prices, corporate earnings and the upcoming Fed decision. The S&P's 52-week high is 7,844.52, set on 6 Oct. (CNBC.)
- **28 Oct.** I found no cash-session data for today yet.

## US Treasuries and the Federal Reserve

- **Yields.**
  - Monday 26 Oct: 10-year 4.986%, 30-year 5.299%, 2-year 4.716%. (CNBC.)
  - Tuesday 27 Oct: 10-year 4.995%, 30-year 5.309%, 2-year 4.737% intraday. (CNBC.) One outlet reported the 10-year fell back to 4.979%. (cryptonews.net.)
  - Wednesday 28 Oct, early: 10-year 5.0134%, 2-year 4.7494%, 30-year 5.32%. (CNBC, 5:22 a.m. EDT.)
- **Fed decision, today.** The FOMC statement is due at 2 p.m. ET on 28 Oct (18:00 UTC), and Chair Kevin Warsh holds a news conference at 2:30 p.m. ET. The decision was not out at the time of writing.
- **Market pricing.** Traders priced a 90.6% chance of no change in the 3.75%–4.00% target range. The probability of a 25-basis-point hike at the 9 Dec meeting stood at 76.5%. (CNBC, 28 Oct.)
- **Next data.** The PCE inflation index is due Thursday 29 Oct. (CNBC, 27 Oct.)

**Gaps.** I found no EIA or API inventory figures for this week and no confirmed Brent settlement for 27–28 Oct. I had no search results on the Fed decision, the 28 Oct equity session, or OPEC+ demand forecasts.

# Brief for Thursday 29 October 2026 (window: since Tuesday 27 October, 13:18 UTC)

## Crude oil (Brent and WTI)

**Prices**
- On Wednesday 28 Oct, Brent settled at $115.32 a barrel, up 1.3%. WTI closed at $102.78, up 2.9%. (The National, 29 Oct)
- On Thursday, oil declined as traders assessed new diplomatic efforts aimed at averting possible US military action against Iran. Brent slipped to $114.10 at 7:48am UAE time. (The National, 29 Oct)
- Brent gained about 11% during October and reached its highest level since April. (UNN, 29 Oct)

**Iran and the Strait of Hormuz**
- On Thursday, Iran's Revolutionary Guards said three oil tankers had caught fire after hitting mines while trying to cross the Strait of Hormuz. The IRGC Navy said they were crossing an unauthorized southern route and were abandoned on the strait's southern shores. This is Iran's own account (Gulf News and Mehr News, 29 Oct). I found no independent confirmation.
- Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Wednesday that Tehran was discussing with mediators how to implement a seven-day plan to end the war and reopen the strait. Iran has also demanded the unfreezing of its assets abroad, the lifting of sanctions on its oil sector, and an end to the US naval blockade. (Gulf News, 29 Oct)
- Tehran rejected reported Qatari peace proposals as unacceptable, but said talks with mediators continue. The US has reportedly warned regional allies to prepare for possible strikes against Iran after the 3 November midterm elections. (Gulf News, 29 Oct)
- On Tuesday 27 Oct, the Iran-aligned Houthis launched a ballistic missile toward the Ras Tanura refinery in eastern Saudi Arabia, the kingdom's largest. (FXStreet, 28 Oct)

**OPEC+**
- Sunday's OPEC+ meeting is expected to keep December output targets unchanged, according to Reuters sources. (FXStreet, 28 Oct) I found no decision yet.

**US inventories**
- EIA data showed US crude inventories (excluding the SPR) fell 1.9 million bbl in the week ended 23 Oct, to 410.6 million bbl, which is 4% below the 5-year average. (OGJ, 28 Oct)
- Sources disagree on the size of the draw. FXStreet reported 1.462 million barrels. Gasoline inventories rose 3.9 million bbl. Distillates fell 1.5 million bbl and are 10% below the 5-year average.

**Demand:** I found nothing new beyond the EIA product-supplied data. Total product supplied averaged 20.8 million b/d over four weeks, up 0.2% year over year.

## Gold

- Spot gold was $4,053.16 an ounce at 9:00 a.m. ET on 28 Oct, slightly above Tuesday's $4,023.02 at the same time. (CNBC, 28 Oct)
- On 29 Oct at 8:22 a.m. ET, APMEX showed spot at $4,063.20, down 0.56% over 24 hours. BullionVault showed about $4,024–4,032 at 12:09 GMT on 29 Oct. Quotes differ by provider.
- For context, gold's record high was $5,602.22 an ounce on 28 January 2026. (APMEX)
- I found no gold-specific news or driver in this window beyond price quotes.

## US equities (S&P 500)

- The S&P 500 closed 0.28% higher on Wednesday 28 Oct at 7,743.98. (MarketScreener, 29 Oct) The Dow was at 52,475.10 and the Nasdaq Composite at 26,549.85. (MSN) One outlet (Bloomingbit) gave a different S&P close of 7,750.88, up 0.37%.
- The S&P 500 and Nasdaq each gained almost 0.3% after the Fed held rates, their third straight daily gain. It was the first time the S&P 500 closed higher on a Fed decision day since December 2025. (CNN, 28 Oct)
- After hours, Fortinet and Alphabet fell. (StockTitan, 28 Oct)
- I did not find a Thursday cash-session close, because the US session had not yet opened at the time of search.

## US Treasuries and the Fed

- **Decision:** The FOMC held the federal funds target range at 3.75%–4.00% on 28 Oct, by a 10–2 vote. Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack dissented, preferring a quarter-point hike. The Fed raised rates in September and held in October.
- **Statement:** The Fed now describes economic activity as growing at a "strong" pace, compared with "solid" in September. (CNN)
- **Meeting schedule:** Chair Kevin Warsh said that from 2027 one of the eight yearly meetings will focus exclusively on policy strategy. (CNBC, 28 Oct)
- **Yields on 28 Oct:** The 10-year was 5.026%, the 2-year 4.704% and the 30-year 5.354%. (CNBC) Trading Economics put the 10-year at 5.00% on 29 Oct. I could not verify that page's timestamp.
- **Rate expectations:** CME FedWatch put the probability of a 25 bp hike at the 9 December meeting at 85.7%. (CNBC, 28 Oct)

**Not found:** no new OPEC+ decision yet, no independent confirmation of the tanker incidents, and no demand data beyond the EIA weekly report.

# Brief: Friday 30 October 2026, 13:18 UTC
Window: since Wednesday 28 October, 13:18 UTC. Sources are listed with each item. Where sources conflict, I say so.

## Crude oil (Brent and WTI)

**Prices**
- Wednesday 28 Oct (CNBC): Brent rose 1.3% to close at $115.32 a barrel, and WTI gained 2.9% to settle at $102.78.
- Thursday 29 Oct: sources conflict.
  - One report (via HDFC Sky) puts the settlement at $114.88 for Brent and $102 for WTI.
  - Another page lists the Oct 29 Brent close as 109.71 USD/bbl. That is far from the other figures, so treat it with caution.
- Friday 30 Oct, morning: Brent was up about 2.1% at $117.19 and WTI up 1.8% at $103.88 by 09:45 GMT (CoinCentral). That is Brent's highest level since late April.
- Monthly move (CNBC, 30 Oct): Brent was on course to finish October about 13% higher, and WTI about 15% higher. It would be the fourth straight monthly gain.
- An Investing.com page reports WTI falling to a session low of $100.25 on reports of direct US–Iran contact. It is undated, and I could not match it to the Friday morning prices above.

**Iran, Hormuz and the region**
- 28 Oct (CNBC): The US is reportedly preparing to renew strikes against Iran after the midterm elections. Strikes could follow the November 3 midterms.
- 29 Oct (AP via Washington Times): Iran said, citing the Revolutionary Guard, that three oil tankers exploded and caught fire after striking naval mines while attempting to transit an unauthorized route in the Strait of Hormuz. The report did not identify the tankers or give casualty details.
- 30 Oct (CNBC): A tanker in the Strait of Hormuz was hit by explosive devices attached by a small boat, UKMTO said. It was not immediately clear who was behind it.
- 30 Oct (CNBC): Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis stepped up attacks on Saudi Arabia.

**OPEC+**
- Seven OPEC+ producers are set to meet Sunday (1 Nov) to review market conditions and production policy (CoinCentral, 30 Oct). I found no reporting on what they are expected to decide.

**US inventories** (EIA, released Wednesday 28 Oct, week ended 23 Oct; Reuters)
- Crude fell by 1.9 million barrels to 410.6 million, against a Reuters poll for a 15,000-barrel rise.
- Gasoline rose by 3.9 million barrels. Distillates fell by 1.5 million barrels.
- Refinery utilization fell 0.6 percentage points to 92.8%.
- Gulf Coast crude stocks fell to their lowest level since December 2024.

**Demand:** I found nothing new specific to oil demand.

## Gold
- Thursday 29 Oct (Voice of Emirates): Spot gold fell 0.7% to $4,039.26 an ounce, with the outlet citing a stronger US dollar.
- Friday 30 Oct, morning: gold was lower again.
  - Kitco showed $3,938.50 an ounce at 9:12 a.m. ET, down $82.00 on the day.
  - APMEX showed $3,982.00, down 1.9%, at 8:30 a.m. ET.
  - BullionVault showed $3,962.74 at 12:17 GMT.
- Silver was down 3.8% at $50.90 in the APMEX quote.
- I found no source explaining Friday's drop.

## US equities (S&P 500)
- Thursday 29 Oct close: The S&P 500 slipped 0.3% to 7,720.39, snapping a three-day advance, while the Nasdaq Composite shed 1.38% to 26,184.72. The Dow lost 132.54 points to 52,342.56. (CNBC)
- Cause: Alphabet's Q3 earnings sparked a sell-off in the stock and AI jitters returned (Yahoo Finance). Alphabet fell about 13% after its third-quarter results, steeper than any session since it went public in 2004. Communication services dropped more than 6% and information technology slid more than 1%.
- Microsoft (Schwab, 29 Oct): it topped analysts' expectations for both earnings per share and revenue.
- Macro data (Schwab, 29 Oct): September PCE inflation came in as expected at 3.6% year on year, and 3.1% for core. Q3 GDP rose 3.4% against 3.2% expected.
- Amazon was due to report after Thursday's close (Yahoo Finance). I found no result for it.
- I found no reliable report on Friday 30 Oct's US session.

## US Treasuries and the Federal Reserve
- Fed decision, Wednesday 28 Oct (CNBC): The central bank held its key interest rate in a range between 3.75% and 4%. Trading Economics notes this followed a 25bp hike in September, the first increase since 2023.
- Trading Economics describes the Fed as having offered limited guidance on its next policy move.
- 10-year yield:
  - Wednesday 28 Oct: 5.05% (FRED).
  - Thursday 29 Oct: 4.937% (CNBC), below 5% after the GDP and inflation data.
  - Friday 30 Oct: 4.91%, down 0.03 points from the previous session (Trading Economics). The same site headlines it as a seven-week low.
- Thursday 29 Oct, other maturities (CNBC): The 2-year lost more than 10 basis points to 4.629%, and the 30-year fell more than 5 basis points to 5.31%.
- Ahead of the meeting (CNBC, 27 Oct): Fed funds futures priced a nearly 93% chance of a hold, per CME FedWatch.

## Gaps and caveats
- Oil price sources disagree on Thursday's settlement. Several pages are undated or have unreliable timestamps.
- I found no confirmed Friday close for any market, because it is still mid-day Friday.
- I found no news on oil demand, and no reporting on OPEC+ expectations for the 1 Nov meeting.
